messages:
Raj: Hey team — we started seeing very odd output from the rerank endpoint when using the Python SDK. All scores are 0 or tiny negative numbers, but when I call the same payload via curl (raw REST) I get sensible positive scores. Case #12345.
Maya: Ugh. Sorry about that — can you paste the SDK version and a minimal repro? Also: did you try pinning to an older client?
Raj: SDK versions: python redwood-sdk==1.3.2, ts client 1.3.2 as well (we use both in different services). Minimal repro below (sanitized):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="***")
items = ["doc A", "doc B", "doc C"]
query = "Find best match"
resp = client.rerank.rerank(query=query, candidates=items)
print(resp.scores)  # returns [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
```
Raj: curl HTTP proxy test: same payload as above (JSON) -> returns [0.42, 0.19, 0.92] which looks correct.
Maya: Thanks. Can you paste the raw payload the SDK sends (or server logs) if available? If not, we can try to reproduce here.
Raj: I captured the outgoing request with our proxy: it looks like the SDK is sending this body: 
```json
{"query":"Find best match","candidates":"[\"doc A\", \"doc B\", \"doc C\"]"}
```
Raj: Note candidates is a stringified list rather than a JSON array. When I send as a proper array it works.
Sam: Oof — that explains it. Thanks for the repro. That matches a serialization bug we introduced when normalizing candidate arrays in 1.3.2. We're coercing arrays to strings in some language bindings when the input is a Python list subclass or when the object has a __str__ override.
Priya: From the backend logs I can see requests with content-type application/json but a string in the candidates field; reranker falls back to default scoring (zero/neutral) when parsing fails, which matches the customer symptom.
Sam: Quick triage: repro'd locally with redwood-sdk==1.3.2, sending list of native str works if I wrap list with list(), but fails if the list is a custom subclass (we didn't sanitize list-like objects). E.g.
```python
class MyList(list):
    pass

client.rerank.rerank(query, candidates=MyList(["a","b"]))  # broken
client.rerank.rerank(query, candidates=["a","b"])  # ok
```
Sam: TS client had a parallel bug where arrays coming from some frameworks (immutable.js lists) were stringified. We have a quick fix: ensure we call JSON serializer that treats sequence protocol, not just isinstance(Array).
Maya: For the customer, short-term workaround?
Sam: Two options: 1) Cast candidates to a plain list/array before passing to the SDK (e.g., list(candidates) in Python or Array.from(candidates) in TS). 2) Use raw HTTP call to /v1/rerank with correct JSON body.
Maya: Got it. I passed the workaround to Raj. He replied: "casting fixed it, thanks — but this is blocking our rollout, can you patch?"
Sam: We're preparing a patch release 1.3.3 that forces array normalization for both Python and TS clients. Will add tests for list subclasses and immutable collections. Targeting an emergency release in the next 6 hours.
Priya: Also note the rerank API has a soft limit of 512 candidates; we should add clearer client-side validation to return an immediate error when >512 to avoid confusing parsing/score fallbacks.
Sam: Agreed. I'll add validation + unit tests.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued for redwood-sdk@1.3.3 -> canary edge (owners: @sam).
Sam: Rolling out canary now. I'll post the release link and changelog when done.
Maya: Raj, we'll push the fix to PyPI/NPM and follow up here. Do you want us to patch your production environment ASAP?
Raj: Yes please — we can accept a fast patch. Also: can you add a note to the SDK docs about candidate type expectations? We had assumed any list-like would work.
Sam: Absolutely — adding docs + changelog. Also adding a migration note: "If you use custom list subclasses or immutable lists, convert to a native list/array or upgrade to 1.3.3+."
Priya: Follow-up: backend will emit a clearer 422 if candidates JSON parsing fails instead of silently falling back; I've filed backend ticket INF-4521. That should prevent silent zero scores for malformed payloads.
Maya: Thanks all. Marking support ticket as "escalated to eng" and will keep case open until Raj confirms 1.3.3 resolves it in prod.
Raj: Confirmed — 1.3.3 fixed it in our staging after you pushed. Scores now match curl test. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :tada:
Maya: Awesome. Closing the loop here — will add a KB entry titled "Rerank: SDK serialization bug (1.3.2) - workaround and fix" and link to the release.
Sam: Linking PR & release: https://github.com/redwood/relevant/pull/423 (patch) and https://pypi.org/project/redwood-sdk/1.3.3
Priya: I'll monitor server logs for any new 422s and follow up if anything else crops up.
Maya: Thanks everyone.
